entries.text_de:
British Museum Cotton Domitian VIII. Die Blätter 95—110, zwei mit dem Rest des Bandes21 nicht zusammenhängende Lagen, um 1140, enthalten Quadr.22, u. S. 529. Diese Handschrift, oder ihre Vorlage oder eine gleichlautende Schwesterhandschrift, stammt aus Worcester. Auf f. 97 beginnt I. II Cnut, u. S. 279; f. 107 Af-Ine, u. S. 17. Dieser Theil bricht ab in Af 2, s. u. S. 4915.

Nicht damit zusammenhängt f. 118, vom Ende 12. Jhs., CHn cor bis c. 6, 1, u. S. 521; der Schreiber liess die Rückseite des Blattes leer.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Cotton Domitian VIII. Leaves 95—110, two gatherings not connected with the rest of the volume21, c. 1140, contain Quadr.22, below, p. 529. This MS, or its exemplar, or a sister MS of identical wording, comes from Worcester. On f. 97 begins I. II Cnut, below, p. 279; f. 107 Af-Ine, below, p. 17. This part breaks off in Af 2, see below, p. 4915.

Not connected with it is f. 118, from the end of the 12th century, CHn cor as far as c. 6, 1, below, p. 521; the scribe left the back of the leaf blank.

wormald.laws: Quadripartitus: Dedicatio, Argumentum, I–II Cn, Af… (breaking off) (Table 4.7, p. 240)
wormald.laws_liebermann: Quadr, I Cn, II Cn, Af, Ine, CHn cor
wormald.other_contents: Only its first two quires survive; two-column layout (p. 254); scribes reproduce amendments (glosses, deletions) evidently from the archetype; alone preserves the 'Dedicatio'; adds rubrics for Alfred's Mosaic introduction (pp. 238–9, 242, 244).
wormald.overview: The earliest surviving Quadripartitus manuscript, written in the second quarter of the twelfth century, perhaps in the West Midlands, and now reduced to two quires holding the prefaces, Cnut and the start of Alfred. Wormald rates it the most important copy despite its brevity, because its scribes reproduce amendments evidently taken from the archetype and because it alone keeps the first preface (the Dedicatio), which he uses to argue that all the versions are one author's work.
wormald.key_quote: Dm (1), the earliest of the series, is also the most important despite lacking all but its first two quires. (p. 238)
wormald.doubts: OCR read 'Domitian vii'; image confirms 'Domitian viii', matching guide. Wormald gives ff. 96r–110v; guide (Liebermann) ff. 95–110. In Wormald's order of recensions Dm is third (after London and R), though earliest copy (p. 243).
